title: Sitting Around Our Father's Board
description: Sitting Around Our Father's Board in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book III, prepared for the Lord's Supper, hymn 23, headed “Grace and glory by the death of Christ”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Sit-ting a-round our Fa-ther's board We raise our tune-ful breath; Our faith be-holds her dy-ing Lord, And dooms our sins to death.

lines: Our faith beholds her dying Lord,
And dooms our sins to death.
We see the blood of Jesus shed,
The sinner views th' atonement made,
Thy cruel thorns, thy shameful cross
Our highest gain springs from thy loss,
Should equal sufferings bear for thee,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
